notes: PDF read successfully via PyMuPDF (3 pages, text-based, not scanned). The Read tool failed (poppler not installed) but text extraction worked. This paper (Pydi et al., Andhra Medical College, Visakhapatnam; Int J Curr Pharm Res 2024) does NOT contain any numeric antibiogram table. Table 1 gives isolate counts/percentages (n=858 total: 839 GNB + 19 GPC); Table 2 is a comparative isolate-frequency table vs other studies; Fig. 1 gives MDR isolate counts per organism. NO per-organism per-antibiotic %S or %R values are printed anywhere, so every organism has an empty drugs array (counts recorded as metadata only). The only susceptibility info is QUALITATIVE and applies to the pooled MDR-GNB subset (177/839 = 20.62% MDR), NOT to individual organisms: MDR GNB were resistant to cephalosporins (ceftazidime, cefixime, ceftriaxone, ceftazidime+clavulanic acid), carbapenems (imipenem, meropenem), and quinolones (ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, nalidixic acid, ofloxacin, levofloxacin), and 'most were sensitive to fosfomycin and nitrofurantoin.' issues: The source paper contains NO per-organism per-drug antibiotic susceptibility table (no %S or %R values). It only reports isolate counts (Table 1), an MDR breakdown (Fig. 1), and a comparative isolate-frequency table (Table 2). Susceptibility is described only qualitatively in prose. The extraction's empty drugs[] arrays correctly reflect this — no susceptibility cells were fabricated.

Organism counts all match Table 1 exactly: E. coli 435, Klebsiella 232, Acinetobacter 105, Pseudomonas 55, Proteus 10, Citrobacter 2, Staph aureus 17, Enterococcus 2. Specimen (urine) and study period (Aug 2022 - Jan 2023) also correct.

Naming over-specification (not in source, an unsupported inference): source lists genus/'spp' level only. Extraction names 'Klebsiella pneumoniae' (source: 'Klebsiella spp'), 'Acinetobacter baumannii' (source: 'Acinetobacter spp'), 'Pseudomonas aeruginosa' (source: 'Pseudomonas spp'), 'Proteus mirabilis' (source: 'Proteus spp'). No susceptibility data hangs off these names, so no clinical impact,
